title: OCR routing ignores provider readiness before execution
reasoning: The router exposes readiness as provider presence, provider.is_ready, and a closed circuit, and its unavailable message reports a distinct not-ready state. However analyze_image only rejects missing providers, open circuits, and disabled providers before calling provider.analyze_image. An enabled but not-ready OCR provider is therefore invoked directly instead of producing the structured ProviderUnavailableError promised by the router's own readiness surface. This can turn a deterministic routing/state error into provider-specific failures or undefined behavior.
reproduction: Create an OCR provider with enabled=True, is_ready=False, and an analyze_image method that records calls. OcrRouter(provider).is_ready is false and unavailable_error_message says not ready, but await analyze_image(...) still calls the provider.
recommendation: In OcrRouter.analyze_image, after the enabled check and before provider.analyze_image, reject providers whose is_ready is false with ProviderUnavailableError using the existing not-ready message semantics.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature, and the excerpt has no regression asserting that is_ready gates analyze_image execution.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an OCR router test with enabled=True and is_ready=False asserting analyze_image raises ProviderUnavailableError and does not call provider.analyze_image.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/core/inference/ocr_router.py plus a focused OCR router unit test.
